sector_verification_note: The most heavily Tier A sector in the taxonomy — the mirror image of Sector 1, where nothing is licensed. 18 of 20 professions name a statutory licensing body. Two verified facts shape everything: NEET applies equally to government, private AND deemed colleges, so there is NO private bypass for medicine; and the NCAHP Act 2021 moved allied health from unregulated to statutorily licensed, making physiotherapy, optometry, MLT and the imaging and OT technologist roles Tier A rather than open-market.

professions.one_liner: Diagnoses and treats illness — the person you see when something is wrong.

deviating_roles.why: Psychiatry and general practice are conversation-led and depend on reading a person over time. Surgery and radiology in the same profession are spatial, procedural and largely wordless.

ai_exposure.reason: Diagnostic support is improving fast and will change the work, but a registered human must examine, decide and carry liability. Physical examination and procedures are not text problems.

nuances.statement: Cost is BIMODAL, not a range. A government seat costs roughly 1-5 lakh for the whole degree; a private or deemed seat costs 60 lakh to 1.2 crore. The figure shown is a blend and describes almost nobody. Which side of that line a student lands on is decided entirely by their NEET rank.
There is NO private bypass. Unlike engineering, money cannot open a door NEET has closed — the same eligibility applies to government, private and deemed colleges alike.

Null because NEET has no upper age limit and no cap on attempts. A commerce graduate is not permanently blocked — they can add PCB through NIOS and sit NEET at any age. It is a long cost, roughly 8 years, not a closed door.

admin_review.reason: The bimodal cost is the single most consequential number in this dataset and the schema cannot express it — one field, two realities 20x apart. Verify actual government vs private MBBS fee ranges and decide how to present them before shipping.

ai_exposure.reason: THE MOST AI-EXPOSED PROFESSION IN THIS SECTOR by a wide margin. The work is mapping documented text to a code set using rules — retrievable knowledge plus digital execution, with almost no physical or clarity component. Auditing and denial management survive longer than routine coding.

admin_review.reason: Very high AI exposure in a sector where everything else is protected. This is a large Indian employment category — healthcare BPOs employ hundreds of thousands — so calling it exposed is a consequential claim. It is also one of very few healthcare careers open to a non-PCB student, which makes removing it costly for that audience. Needs a human decision.

Wellness rather than clinical treatment. BNYS naturopathy doctors are a separate question — see boundary notes.
All writing professions share one parent.
PROVISIONAL — counselling families through a diagnosis. Very small in India; flagged for review.

boundary_decisions_needing_your_signoff: AYURVEDA and HOMEOPATHY are separate professions because they have separate statutory councils — NCISM and NCH. Unani and Siddha are folded into Ayurveda as job roles since they share NCISM. BNYS (naturopathy and yoga) is currently NOT included; it is small and sits awkwardly between this sector and Sector 18. Needs your call.

MEDICAL CODER is the only high AI-exposure profession here and one of the only healthcare careers open to a non-PCB student. Removing it would close the sector almost entirely to commerce and arts students.

PUBLIC HEALTH PROFESSIONAL is mid_stream_entry 'after_any_degree' — the MPH accepts statistics, social science and management graduates. This is the sector's main door for non-medical students and was flagged during Sector 3 as needing a home.

NURSE is the clearest 'pathway: any' case in the dataset — Gulf, UK and Ireland recruit Indian nurses at scale and pay differs several-fold. Confirm how prominently international routes should be surfaced.
DENTIST carries a known oversupply problem in India. Listed with a high-priority review rather than quietly omitted.

1.0: Initial build. 20 professions; 18 name a statutory licensing body.

NCAHP Act 2021 is the biggest single finding — allied health is now Tier A, not open-market.
Kept both promises made to this sector: Biomedical Equipment Technician (from Sector 2) and Medical Laboratory Technologist (from Sector 3).
